findings.title: Staleness handling depends on an undefined commit-distance calculation
findings.description: The preconditions require reporting commit drift “including the commit distance” when `meta.json`’s `gitCommitHash` differs from `HEAD`, but the design does not define how to calculate that distance when the analyzed commit is not an ancestor of `HEAD`, is unavailable locally, or belongs to a different history. In those cases, a simple revision count may fail or be misleading. Specify the comparison semantics and behavior when distance cannot be established; otherwise this required warning can itself fail or give false confidence.

findings.title: Capability 2 promises interview-sourced content without defining an interview
findings.description: The Inputs section says that without a concept, the skill sources purpose from the initiative plan “plus interview.” But Capability 2 defines no interview flow, and the translation rules say every claim must trace to an input artifact. This leaves the common no-concept path without a specified source for missing purpose, problem, or audience facts—and no rule for whether to ask the PM or mark them unknown. Define that interaction or remove interview as an assumed input.

findings.title: Analysis index allocation is neither bounded nor collision-safe
findings.description: The document assigns generated outputs the remaining 940–949 slots, then permits overflow into the heavily used 900 band “as needed,” but specifies no allocator, collision check, or behavior when those indices are already occupied. This affects both comprehension output and overview output, and repeated or concurrent runs can overwrite an existing artifact or claim an index used by another analysis. Define a deterministic reservation/selection rule and whether runs create new samples or update prior outputs.

findings.title: Graph input validation and incompatible plugin output are unspecified
findings.description: The architecture depends on a detailed upstream graph shape and named fields, but only specifies behavior for a missing graph—not malformed, partial, or newer-version output. For example, absent `tour[]`, unknown node types, or unreadable `meta.json` could undermine the structural extraction or staleness provenance while the workflow still drafts documents. Define the minimum supported contract and explicit failure/degraded behavior for invalid or incompatible inputs.
